source.subject: Let Track Work work in repositories reached through a symlink

seed.description: In assertGitSafePath, the record-path side of the Git-safety comparison is no longer canonicalized: relative(repositoryRoot, canonicalPath(path)) became relative(repositoryRoot, resolve(path)), while the repository root stays canonical because Git reports canonical paths. createRecordPath passes the unresolved .freeflow/tasks path, which does not exist yet, so under a symlinked directory the relative path climbs out of the repository with ../ segments, check-ignore cannot match it, and init refuses it. This is a realistic simplification (dropping the helper on one side of a comparison) and it breaks the commit's own symlink test, which runs init first.

seed_verification.seeded_result: 29 pass, 1 fail: a repository reached through a symlinked directory works like any other
seed_verification.evidence: The failing assertion is the init step (exitCode expected 0): the error is 'Record path is not ignored by Git' (unignored-path), with the .freeflow/tasks path reported as ../ segments relative to the canonical repository root.
